record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: If p is k-avoidable then there are circular words with length |p| on k letters that avoid p.

evidence.quote: If p is k-avoidable then there are circular words with length |p| on k letters that avoid p.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let A be a finite alphabet and let E be a separate set of symbols called pattern variables. A pattern is a nonempty word p ∈ E^+; its length |p| is its number of letters as a word over E. A word w ∈ A^* is said to encounter p if there exists a non-erasing morphism h : E^+ → A^+ such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w avoids p. A circular word of length n on A is an equivalence class of words in A^n under cyclic rotation, equivalently a word read on a cycle of n positions; a circular word w avoids p if no factor of w (taken cyclically, i.e., no factor of ww of length at most n) encounters p.

A pattern p is said to be k-avoidable if there exist infinitely many (equivalently, arbitrarily long) words over a k-letter alphabet that avoid p.

Conjecture. Prove or disprove: for every pattern p and every integer k ≥ 1, if p is k-avoidable, then for every sufficiently large integer n there exists a circular word of length n on a k-letter alphabet that avoids p.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface related results on circular words avoiding patterns (e.g., Currie's work showing binary cube-free circular words of every length, and results on the circular repetition threshold), but no source explicitly resolves the general conjecture that k-avoidability of a pattern p implies existence of arbitrarily long circular words on k letters avoiding p. The status appears to remain open in the literature consulted.

status_evidence.title: Circular Words Avoiding Patterns (Currie)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies circular words avoiding patterns; proves binary cube-free circular words exist of every length and lists open problems on circular avoidance.
status_evidence.claim: Provides positive results in special cases but does not establish the general implication for all k-avoidable patterns.

status_evidence.title: Repetition Threshold for Circular Words
status_evidence.snippet: Determines the circular repetition threshold CRT(k) for k ≥ 6.
status_evidence.claim: Related circular-avoidance question solved for repetitions; general pattern conjecture not addressed.
